entities.name: Audrey
entities.description: One of the two speakers, and the dog owner of the pair. She keeps four small mutts — Pepper, Precious, Panda and Pixie — and organises most of her life around them: parks, trails, a training course, agility classes, grooming, a behaviourist and a dog owners group. She moved in June 2023 to a house with a bigger backyard, cooks, keeps a small garden, makes and sells jewellery from recycled objects and donates part of the profits to an animal shelter, and wears tattoos of her dogs on her arm. She was once unable to walk her dogs because of a knee injury, and broke an arm playing with them in October 2023. Her childhood dog was Max.

entities.name: Andrew
entities.description: The other speaker. He started a new job as a Financial Analyst in the week before 27 March 2023 and lives in the same city as Audrey with his girlfriend. Nature is the thread of everything he says: he hikes, took up rock climbing in June 2023, watches birds, reads about ecosystems and tends balcony flowers, and blames his job and city living for cutting him off from the outdoors. He had no pets in March 2023 and ended 2023 with three dogs — Toby in July, Buddy in October and Scout in November — saying on 4 November 2023 that he had managed to make it work while still living in the city.

entities.name: Andrew's girlfriend
entities.description: Andrew's partner, never named in the conversation and referred to only as 'my girlfriend', 'my GF' and 'my girl'. She appears in roughly half the sessions as his companion on the things he does outside work: cafes, hikes, a picnic, volunteering at a pet shelter, camping with Toby, fishing, a farm visit, a wine tasting, board games, a bike ride, and naming and caring for Scout.

properties.aliases: my girlfriend; my GF; my girl

entities.name: Pepper
entities.description: One of Audrey's dogs, and one of the three she had already had for about three years in March 2023. Pepper took a while to accept the puppy Pixie in spring 2023 and afterwards the two were inseparable. Pepper's favourite resting place is the couch. Audrey called Pepper a Jack Russell mix or Chihuahua mix in July and September 2023 and a Lab mix on 28 October 2023.

entities.name: Precious
entities.description: One of Audrey's dogs, and one of the three she had already had for about three years in March 2023. Her favourite resting place is her chair. Andrew took her to be the dog whose leash broke at the park on 22 September 2023. Audrey described her as a Jack Russell or Chihuahua mix in mid-2023 and as a Chihuahua mix on 28 October 2023.

entities.name: Panda
entities.description: One of Audrey's dogs, and one of the three she had already had for about three years in March 2023. A male dog whose favourite resting place is his rug. Audrey called him a Jack Russell or Chihuahua mix in July and September 2023 and a Lab mix on 28 October 2023.

entities.name: Pixie
entities.description: The puppy Audrey adopted shortly before 2 April 2023, making her household four dogs. She took a few days to settle with Pepper, Precious and Panda and then became inseparable from them. Her favourite resting place is her own bed. Audrey described her as a Chihuahua mix on 28 October 2023.

entities.name: Andrew's family's dog
entities.description: The dog belonging to Andrew's family, never named. Andrew showed Audrey a photograph of it on a couch on 2 April 2023 and said he misses exploring nature trails with it — the experience he was trying to recover when he set out to get a dog of his own.

entities.name: the city where Audrey and Andrew live
entities.description: The unnamed city both speakers live in. Neither ever names it. They are treated as living in one place because Andrew asks Audrey about keeping dogs 'even with living in the city', both complain about the same shortage of open space, and they plan local outings and a joint hike together. It is the constant background of the conversation: Andrew's difficulty finding a dog-friendly rental, and both of their need to leave it to reach nature.

entities.name: Fox Hollow
entities.description: A hiking trail Andrew recommended to Audrey on 27 March 2023 as a good weekend hike with great views. Audrey said she would try it, and reported on 2 April 2023 that the new puppy had kept her too busy to get there.

entities.name: the park near Audrey's home
entities.description: The unnamed park Audrey walks her dogs in, referred to across the conversation as 'the park' and 'our local park'. She walks them there for about an hour at a time, plays fetch and frisbee, meets other owners for playdates, let them off the leash there on 1 June 2023, broke her arm playing with them there in October 2023, and it is where one of them broke her leash on 22 September 2023. The dog park she uses is right beside it.

properties.aliases: the park; our local park; the park we usually walk

entities.name: the dog park near Audrey's home
entities.description: The unnamed dog park beside the park where Audrey usually walks her dogs, with a big grassy area, trees, shade and benches for owners. She uses it for playdates, describes it as paradise for her dogs, started agility classes with them there in August 2023, and took them there on 30 September 2023.

entities.name: the open space Andrew found to hike
entities.description: An unnamed open space near the city that Andrew found by early May 2023 after weeks of complaining he had nowhere to hike; he called it refreshing, and returned to it with friends and his girlfriend over the weekend of 6-7 May 2023 as 'the spot we found recently'.

properties.aliases: the new open space; the spot we found recently

entities.name: Andrew's employer
entities.description: The firm, never named, where Andrew started work as a Financial Analyst in the week before 27 March 2023. He described it as quite a change from his previous job; from July 2023 onwards the job is what he blames for keeping him indoors and away from hiking, and by September 2023 he called it tough and stressful and said finding balance had been challenging.

entities.name: Audrey's dog training course
entities.description: The positive-reinforcement dog training Audrey undertook in mid-2023. She saw a flyer for it at her local pet store and signed up on or before 11 May 2023 for a pet-bonding workshop in June 2023, and by 3 July 2023 described herself as taking a dog training course that was a big time sink but had already improved her dogs' behaviour. The workshop and the course are recorded as one undertaking because the dates run on and both are positive-reinforcement training of her own dogs; nothing in the conversation separates them. She was still using positive reinforcement in October 2023 on the animal behaviourist's advice.

properties.aliases: the workshop about bonding with my pet; the positive reinforcement training class; the dog training course

entities.name: hiking
entities.description: The activity both speakers care most about and the main subject of the conversation. Andrew hikes to escape the city, aiming for at least one trip a weekend when work allows, and photographs the views; by October 2023 work had made it rare. Audrey hikes with her four dogs, on local trails, in national parks and on road trips. A joint hike with all their dogs was proposed in July 2023 and finally set for Saturday 4 November 2023.

entities.name: birdwatching
entities.description: Andrew's long-standing interest: he has never gone out specifically to birdwatch but spots birds while hiking, and says eagles mesmerise him. On 1 October 2023 Audrey said she wanted to take it up, was working from a birdwatching guide book and meant to learn the common birds in her area, and Andrew offered advice, his binoculars and a notebook and proposed they go together.

entities.name: Andrew's search for a dog and a dog-friendly home
entities.description: The undertaking that runs from April to November 2023: Andrew wanting a dog of his own, and needing a place in the city that would allow one. He browsed websites, visited shelters, asked friends, contacted landlords and walked neighbourhoods, wanting somewhere near a park or woods. He was still without a place in September 2023, took Toby home in July anyway, and by 4 November 2023 said he had managed to make it work with dogs while still living in the city.

entities.name: Audrey's dog tattoos
entities.description: The tattoos on Audrey's arm depicting her dogs, alongside sunflowers. She had the first done before April 2023 and said it represents her love for her dogs and for nature's beauty and lets her see their faces when they are not with her; she added a second tattoo of all four dogs in August 2023 and had more drawing added at the tattoo parlour in October 2023, saying that was enough unless she ever got another dog.

entities.name: Max
entities.description: Audrey's childhood dog, an energetic dog who loved a game of fetch. She took long walks with him around the neighbourhood as a child, exploring new paths and confiding her worries and hopes in him, and described those days on 27 July 2023 as some of her favourite memories.

entities.name: Toby
entities.description: Andrew's first dog, a German Shepherd puppy he took home shortly before 11 July 2023 despite living in the city. Andrew describes him as active and fond of sweaters, took him camping in August 2023, and said in September 2023 that he was still too young to take hiking. Buddy joined him in October 2023 and Scout in November 2023, and Toby needed time to get used to each of them.

entities.name: Audrey's new house
entities.description: The house with a bigger backyard that Audrey had moved into by 26 June 2023, announced as 'a new place with a bigger backyard for the pooches'. She set up a doggy play area there with agility equipment and toys, and was still unpacking boxes at the end of June 2023.

properties.aliases: my new place; the new house

entities.name: the lake in the mountains Audrey found on a hike
entities.description: An unnamed lake in the mountains that Audrey and her friends came across on a hike a few years before 2023. She described it twice — on 26 June 2023 and again on 24 August 2023 — as somewhere they sat, talked and admired the peacefulness, and said she would never forget it. It is her answer both times to what nature at its most calming means to her.

properties.aliases: this stunning lake in the mountains; a gorgeous lake in the mountains

entities.name: Audrey's dog agility classes
entities.description: The agility classes Audrey started with her four dogs at a dog park in early August 2023, separate from her earlier positive-reinforcement training. She takes them twice a week for practice and calls it a physical and mental workout for them and a bonding experience for all of them, as well as a way for them to build relationships with other dogs.

entities.name: the pet shelter Andrew volunteered at
entities.description: An unnamed pet shelter where Andrew and his girlfriend volunteered on Monday 24 July 2023. He called it one of the most rewarding things he had ever done and their way of giving back, and it reinforced how much he wanted animals of his own.

entities.name: rock climbing
entities.description: The sport Andrew took up on Sunday 11 June 2023, when he and friends took a class and he reached the top. He called himself a newbie, said he was hooked, and said it had encouraged him to try more outdoor activities such as kayaking and possibly bungee jumping.

entities.name: cooking
entities.description: A shared interest the two speakers discovered on 3 July 2023. Audrey has long loved it, calling it an escape, self-care and a way to let her creativity flow; her favourites are Chicken Pot Pie, a family recipe, and Roasted Chicken with Mediterranean flavours, and garlic is her go-to ingredient. Andrew took it up in mid-2023 as something to do while he could not hike, and said it helps him de-stress and be creative.

entities.name: Audrey's dog grooming course
entities.description: The course Audrey took to learn to groom her dogs herself, the new skill she reported on 19 August 2023. From it she learned to groom slowly and gently, to take care over sensitive areas such as ears and paws, and to stay patient and positive; she passed those tips to Andrew for Toby.

entities.name: gardening
entities.description: Something both speakers took to in 2023. Audrey keeps a small garden with flowers — Peruvian Lilies, which she says need only water and sun — and a vegetable patch coming along, and her dogs run about in it. Andrew was tending a balcony full of flowers by 24 September 2023, and in October 2023 Audrey suggested he get more plants for his home as a way of keeping some contact with nature in the city.

entities.name: Buddy
entities.description: The second dog Andrew adopted, from a shelter, shortly before 19 October 2023. Andrew named him Buddy because he is his buddy and because he hoped he and Toby would become buddies. The two of them go for walks together and Buddy enjoys checking out new hiking trails.

entities.name: Scout
entities.description: The third dog Andrew adopted, shortly before 22 November 2023, a fortnight after saying he would look after the two he had before getting more. He and his girlfriend took a while to settle on the name Scout, which they chose for the pup's adventurous spirit, and were keeping the new arrival on a leash outdoors while it got used to things.

entities.name: Audrey's dog owners group
entities.description: The group of dog owners Audrey joined shortly before 4 November 2023 to learn how to take better care of her dogs. She meets them about once a week, for tips from other owners and so that all the dogs can play together, and suggested Andrew consider joining one.

entities.name: the animal shelter Audrey donates to
entities.description: An unnamed animal shelter to which Audrey donates a portion of the profits from the jewellery she sells, saying they do great work and it is her way of helping out. It is kept separate from the pet shelter Andrew volunteered at, because nothing in the conversation connects the two.

entities.name: making jewellery from recycled objects
entities.description: Audrey's craft: she hunts down bottle caps, buttons and broken jewellery and turns them into one-of-a-kind pieces, which she says expresses both her creativity and her commitment to sustainability. She began it as a hobby, later started selling her pieces, and donates a portion of the profits to an animal shelter.

entities.name: Audrey's knee injury
entities.description: A knee injury, at an unstated earlier date, that left Audrey unable to walk her dogs. She described it on 6 October 2023 as a tough period because the walks bring her so much joy, and photographed her dogs after she started walking again.

entities.name: Audrey's broken arm
entities.description: The injury Audrey suffered in an accident while playing with her dogs at the park in the week before 24 October 2023, leaving one arm in a cast. She said caring for four dogs one-handed was tricky but that they were managing and that she felt better each day.
